question: Should OpenClaw add an opt-in execute-on-parse scheduler now, and should early execution be blocked until tool concurrency-safety metadata exists?
rationale: This changes core runtime semantics rather than repairing a broken existing contract, and the safest API/default policy depends on maintainer intent around tool safety, approvals, cancellation, and transcript ordering.

options.title: Design after safety contract
options.body: Keep this open and make execute-on-parse depend on explicit tool concurrency-safety metadata or an equivalent scheduler policy.

options.title: Prototype experimental opt-in
options.body: Allow a narrow experimental implementation with tests and real runtime proof, limited to known-safe tools and default-off behavior.

options.title: Decline early scheduling
options.body: Keep the current post-stream tool execution contract and rely on ordinary post-parse parallel batching for now.

recommendation.title: Design after safety contract
recommendation.body: Keep this open and make execute-on-parse depend on explicit tool concurrency-safety metadata or an equivalent scheduler policy.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent ownership signal for the agent-core and reusable AI runtime boundaries involved in this product decision.
